To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Scap/Insig complex is a cholesterol sensor that regulates SREBP processing, that Scap is a cholesterol-binding protein that cooperatively binds cholesterol, and that Insig is a cholesterol sensor for Scap that cooperatively regulates SREBP-1 and SREBP- 2 processing.

Scap cooperatively senses ER cholesterol levels, that Scap cooperativity is modulated by Insig-1 expression, and that Scap cooperates with Insig-1 to control ER cholesterol levels within narrow limits.

1) ER cholesterol is regulated with remarkable precision; 2) ER cholesterol is sensed through cooperative interactions between cholesterol, Insig and Scap; 3) these interactions create a switch-like control of Srebp-2 transport that blocks cholesterol synthesis and uptake when ER cholesterol exceeds a threshold level of 5% of all ER lipids (mol/mol).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of cholesterol homeostasis.
how cells sense the cholesterol composition of their membranes.
the mechanisms that regulate the level of membrane lipids in eukaryotic cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ER membrane cholesterol level of 5% is an optimal level that is required for normal cellular function and is maintained at that level by a feedback mechanism that is sensitive to small changes in the ER cholesterol content.
the cholesterol level in ER membrane is sensed by a cooperative network of Scap and Insig proteins.
the ER membrane cholesterol concentration is tightly regulated, and the Scap/Insig system acts as a cholesterol sensor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cholesterol level of the ER is sensed by Scap and Insig, and that the ER cholesterol level is controlled to maintain the level of SREBPs within a narrow range.
cholesterol homeostasis is regulated by a protein complex that senses ER cholesterol levels and controls SREBP-1c and SREBP- 2 transport to the Golgi apparatus.
ER cholesterol is controlled within a narrow window by a cooperative protein network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Scap is a cholesterol sensor, and that the ER membrane contains a protein network that senses ER cholesterol levels with remarkable precision.
the ER cholesterol level is controlled by a switch-like mechanism that is sensitive to small changes in cholesterol content.
Scap cooperatively binds cholesterol.
